leads.summary: The stock Omarchy Emacs install loses all four universal clipboard chords because it does not define native Super bindings
leads.consequence: A newly installed, uncustomized emacs-wayland window receives Super+A/C/V/X instead of the previous Ctrl+A/C/V/X; its default pgtk/X11 keymaps do not assign those Super chords. Select-all, copy, paste and cut consequently cease to perform their advertised actions in this supported editor. The linked issue's custom Doom shortcuts do not prove all Emacs instances are configured the same way. Not executed live; confirmed by tracing the pinned installer and keymap sources.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Stock Linux Emacs does not bind Super+A/C/V/X, so the default tag leaves them unbound.

### Emacs on Linux has no Super clipboard bindings

GNU Emacs binds `s-a/c/v/x` only in its macOS/GNUstep port, and Doom only on macOS. **Impact:** in stock Emacs, Doom and `omarchy-emacs` the chords arrive unbound; cua-mode users lose copy/cut/paste.

**Suggested change:** fix the `emacs.lua` comment and document Emacs bindings plus the `-native-super-clipboard` opt-out in `manual/07-hotkeys.md`, or leave Emacs untagged.

<details><summary>Source check (no live Emacs)</summary>

# Reproducer: Emacs and Doom bind Super+A/C/V/X only on macOS

Source-level reproduction (no live Emacs was available). It shows that the premise in `default/hypr/apps/emacs.lua` ("Emacs binds the Super chords itself (Doom maps Super+C and Super+V ...)") holds only for macOS builds. On Linux, `s-a`, `s-c`, `s-v` and `s-x` are unbound in GNU Emacs 31.1, in stock Doom Emacs and in the `omarchy-emacs` setup that `omarchy-install-editor-emacs` installs. Once the PR tags every `emacs`/`Emacs` window, Super+A/C/V/X in those setups reach Emacs as unbound keys.

## GNU Emacs 31.1: the only default Super clipboard bindings are in ns-win.el

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse --branch emacs-31.1 https://github.com/emacs-mirror/emacs emacs
cd emacs && git sparse-checkout set lisp
rg -n '\?\\s-[acvx]\]|"s-[acvx]"|\(kbd "s-[acvx]"\)|\[s-[acvx]\]' lisp
sed -n 43,44p lisp/term/ns-win.el
```

Actual output:

```
lisp/term/ns-win.el:116:(define-key global-map [?\s-a] 'mark-whole-buffer)
lisp/term/ns-win.el:117:(define-key global-map [?\s-c] 'ns-copy-including-secondary)
lisp/term/ns-win.el:145:(define-key global-map [?\s-v] 'yank)
lisp/term/ns-win.el:147:(define-key global-map [?\s-x] 'kill-region)
(or (featurep 'ns)
    (error "%s: Loading ns-win.el but not compiled for GNUstep/macOS"
```

`ns-win.el` refuses to load outside the NS (GNUstep/macOS) build. `lisp/term/pgtk-win.el` contains no Super bindings.

## Doom Emacs: the Super bindings sit inside a macOS-only block

The doomemacs master branch (01d68aaf, 2026-09-06) pins its modules submodule at doomemacs/modules d57ab52a.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/doomemacs/modules doom-modules
git -C doom-modules checkout d57ab52a3425b6d39564fb011b0e9571da0e270f
cd doom-modules
rg -n '"s-[acvx]"|\[s-[acvx]\]|\(kbd "s-[acvx]"\)' modules
sed -n 129p modules/config/default/config.el
```

Actual output:

```
modules/config/default/config.el:148:        "s-c" (if (featurep 'evil) #'evil-yank #'copy-region-as-kill)
modules/config/default/config.el:149:        "s-v" #'yank
modules/config/default/config.el:151:        "s-x" (cmds! (doom-region-active-p) #'kill-region
modules/config/default/config.el:160:        "s-a" #'mark-whole-buffer
(when (featurep :system 'macos)
```

The `(when (featurep :system 'macos) ...)` form runs from line 129 to line 181, so all four bindings are inside it. The same block exists at doomemacs/doomemacs ae70a26d (2026-04-24, before the modules moved out), at `modules/config/default/config.el` lines 306 to 358.

## Omarchy's own Emacs setup adds no bindings

`omarchy-install-editor-emacs` installs the AUR package `omarchy-emacs` (1.10.1, `depends=('emacs-wayland' 'bash')`). Its source tarball matches the PKGBUILD sha256 (`c3c106ca...a49`) and contains no key bindings:

```sh
curl -L -o omarchy-emacs.tar.gz https://github.com/scottjones/omarchy-emacs/archive/refs/tags/v1.10.1.tar.gz
tar xzf omarchy-emacs.tar.gz && cd omarchy-emacs-1.10.1
rg -n -i -c 'cua-mode|global-set-key|keymap-global-set|define-key|"s-|kbd ' config bin; echo "rg exit=$?"
```

Actual output:

```
rg exit=1
```

## cua-mode: the Ctrl chords are copy, cut and paste today

`lisp/emulation/cua-base.el` lines 34 to 50 (Emacs 31.1): with cua-mode on, `C-x`, `C-c` and `C-v` are cut, copy and paste. `C-x` and `C-c` act that way only while the region is active. At the base commit, Super+X/C/V reach Emacs as those Ctrl chords. With the PR they arrive as `s-x`/`s-c`/`s-v`, which cua-mode does not bind.

Not verified live: no Emacs binary was available in the sandbox (`emacs: MISSING`), so the resulting "s-c is undefined" message was not observed.
</details>

### Shell panels over Emacs get Super chords

`hl.get_active_window()` keeps the window underneath while a panel has keyboard focus. **Impact:** over Emacs, panel fields (e.g. Wi-Fi password) get Super chords, not Ctrl+A/C/V/X; per Qt source they type the letter (untested).

**Suggested change:** send the Ctrl chords while a shell panel has keyboard focus.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 01d2a64b)</summary>

# Reproducer: a shell panel opened over Emacs gets Super chords instead of the Ctrl chords

The universal clipboard shortcuts send without a window target so that they reach focused layer-shell surfaces such as Omarchy panels (the `clipboard.lua` header and commit a0e6d65b). The PR picks the chord from the tags of `hl.get_active_window()`. In Hyprland 0.56.2 that call returns the last focused window, not the layer surface that has keyboard focus:

- `src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsQuery.cpp:125-134`: `hlGetActiveWindow` returns `Desktop::focusState()->window()`.
- `src/desktop/view/LayerSurface.cpp:201` and `:401`: a layer surface that takes keyboard focus calls `Desktop::focusState()->rawSurfaceFocus(...)`.
- `src/desktop/state/FocusState.cpp:223-261`: `rawSurfaceFocus` sets the seat's keyboard focus and `m_focusSurface`, but leaves `m_focusWindow` unchanged.
- `src/config/shared/actions/ConfigActions.cpp:1530-1599` (`Actions::pass`, reached from `send_key_state` through `Actions::sendKeyState` at 1601-1618): with no window target, `xtract` (line 47) yields no window, the focus switch at 1537-1552 is skipped, and the mods and key at 1554-1576 go to the current keyboard focus, which is the panel.

Omarchy panels with text fields (network passphrase, weather location, clock, tailscale) use Qt Quick Controls `TextField` (`shell/Ui/TextField.qml`); the polkit password uses a plain `TextInput`. Qt 6.11.2 `src/gui/kernel/qplatformtheme.cpp:204-218, 273` binds Cut, Copy, Paste and SelectAll to Ctrl+X/C/V/A (plus dedicated-key, Insert, Delete and Sun-key variants), not to Super+A/C/V/X.

So with an Emacs window focused underneath, the panel receives Super+A/C/V/X, which Qt does not treat as select all, copy, paste or cut. From Qt's source it would insert the letter instead (not verified live). At the base commit it received Ctrl+A/C/V/X: Super+A/X always sent Ctrl, and Emacs was not tagged.

## Standalone test (PR-style stub, prints the chords before the result)

The stub models the Hyprland state above: `get_active_window()` returns the tagged Emacs window, and `get_layers()` lists the panel as mapped with exclusive keyboard interactivity. This is the exact script that produced the outputs below; inside `hyprland-default-config-test.sh` the same check would use the suite's `pass`/`fail` helpers.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer in the style of test/shell.d/hyprland-default-config-test.sh.
# Models what Hyprland 0.56.2 reports while an Omarchy shell panel (a
# layer-shell surface) holds keyboard focus over an Emacs window:
# hl.get_active_window() still returns the Emacs window (FocusState keeps
# m_focusWindow when a layer surface takes focus), and hl.get_layers() lists
# the panel as mapped with keyboard interactivity (1 = exclusive).
# The chord is delivered to the panel, a Qt TextField, where only the Ctrl
# chords are copy/paste/cut/select all.
# Usage: ROOT=<omarchy checkout> bash panel-over-emacs-test.sh
set -u
ROOT="${ROOT:?}"

clipboard_output=$(OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" lua <<'LUA'
local sent, binds = {}, {}
local emacs = { class = "emacs", tags = { "default-opacity*", "native-super-clipboard*" } }
hl = {
  get_active_window = function() return emacs end,
  get_layers = function() return { { namespace = "omarchy-panel", mapped = true, interactivity = 1 } } end,
  dispatch = function(action) if action.state == "down" then table.insert(sent, action.mods .. "+" .. action.key) end end,
  dsp = { send_key_state = function(options) return options end },
  timer = function(callback) callback() end,
}
o = { bind = function(keys, _, dispatcher) binds[keys] = dispatcher end }
dofile(os.getenv("OMARCHY_PATH") .. "/default/hypr/bindings/clipboard.lua")

for _, key in ipairs({ "A", "C", "V", "X" }) do
  sent = {}
  binds["SUPER + " .. key]()
  print("panel-over-emacs " .. key .. " " .. table.concat(sent, ","))
end
LUA
)
expected="panel-over-emacs A CTRL+A
panel-over-emacs C CTRL+C
panel-over-emacs V CTRL+V
panel-over-emacs X CTRL+X"
echo "$clipboard_output"
if [[ $clipboard_output == "$expected" ]]; then
  echo "ok - a shell panel focused over Emacs still gets the Ctrl clipboard chords"
else
  echo "not ok - a shell panel focused over Emacs still gets the Ctrl clipboard chords"
  exit 1
fi
```

Actual output at the base commit (b18ab495):

```
panel-over-emacs A CTRL+A
panel-over-emacs C CTRL+C
panel-over-emacs V CTRL+V
panel-over-emacs X CTRL+X
ok - a shell panel focused over Emacs still gets the Ctrl clipboard chords
```

Actual output at the PR head (01d2a64b):

```
panel-over-emacs A SUPER+A
panel-over-emacs C SUPER+C
panel-over-emacs V SUPER+V
panel-over-emacs X SUPER+X
not ok - a shell panel focused over Emacs still gets the Ctrl clipboard chords
```

Limits: this reproduces the chord choice in Lua against a stub that models Hyprland's focus semantics as read from its source. It was not run in a live Hyprland session with a real panel and Emacs. For Super+C/V, the base code already has the same gap when a terminal is the window underneath: the panel gets Ctrl+Shift+C/V, which Qt does not treat as copy or paste.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- `(emacs|Emacs)` is full-matched by Hyprland and covers pgtk `emacs`, X11 `Emacs` and daemon-created emacsclient frames.
- `send_key_state` writes straight to the seat, so the Super chord cannot re-trigger the Super+C bind.
- Terminals and untagged windows get the same chords as at the base commit for all four keys.
- `emacs.lua` loads from the stock config with no migration; the keybindings menu output is unchanged.
- The new test passes at head and fails against the base `clipboard.lua`.

**Optional test improvement:** no test window carries both `terminal` and `native-super-clipboard`, so a mutant that swaps the two branches still passes. Adding such a row would pin the precedence.

**Related PRs:** #13657 fixes the same issue #13515 with class matching and conflicts with this PR in `clipboard.lua`. #13634 and #13007 edit the same `universal_clipboard_shortcut` code and also conflict textually with this PR.

**Panel fix note:** one untested option is to check `hl.get_layers()` for a shell panel that holds keyboard focus. Keyboard interactivity alone is not enough: `KeyboardPanel.qml` keeps OnDemand focus after focus moves back to a window.

**Docs:** the Emacs-side bindings would be e.g. `(keymap-global-set "s-c" #'kill-ring-save)`, and the opt-out `o.window("(emacs|Emacs)", { tag = "-native-super-clipboard" })` in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` (source-checked, not tested live). `manual/07-hotkeys.md:139` and `manual/03-coming-from-mac-or-windows.md:25` still say the universal clipboard keys work everywhere.
</details>
